name: Madhubani
basis: why/hist: natural pigments painted by women on house walls with twigs; how: eight pigments, black outlines, a pattern fill per pigment
note: Hard call: models the outline-and-fill convention; the wall ground is not modelled. Arguable as no (style).

lumenary.blurb: Mithila painting from Bihar: flat natural pigments, a heavy black line around every shape, and no space left empty, so each colour is filled with its own pattern.

facts.era: Ancient tradition, on paper since the 1960s
facts.bestOn: Pictures with clear shapes and bold colour

why: Madhubani, or Mithila, painting does not like empty space. Every figure is outlined and then filled with a pattern of its own, lines, dots, scales or waves, so that the painting hums with texture. The colours come from natural pigments, and women painted them on the walls of houses, especially for weddings. This treatment does the same by colour: a region of red gets a lattice, a region of yellow gets dots.
how: Blur the picture and snap it to eight pigments: madder red, turmeric, leaf green, indigo, lamp black, paper, saffron and earth.
Clean regions with a majority filter and outline them in black wherever two colours meet.

Choose a fill pattern for each pigment: a diamond lattice on red, dots on yellow, waves on green, fish-scale arcs on blue, dots in paper white on black, concentric rings on saffron and stripes in paper white on earth.
Set the pattern size and strength with the sliders.
Add a double border with its own small motifs, like the decorated edge of a wall painting.
history: Madhubani painting comes from the Mithila region of Bihar and the neighbouring parts of Nepal, painted with twigs and cotton-wrapped sticks and with pigments from turmeric, indigo, soot, flowers and clay. After the Bihar earthquake of 1934 the British officer William Archer photographed wall paintings in damaged houses. From the 1960s women artists such as Sita Devi, Ganga Devi and Mahasundari Devi brought the art onto paper, and it became known across India and abroad.
terms: The cultural region in Bihar and Nepal where Madhubani art began.
Colour made from plants, minerals and soot.
The urge to fill every empty space in an artwork.
paragraphs: Madhubani, or Mithila, painting comes from the Mithila region of Bihar and the neighbouring parts of Nepal. Women painted it on the walls of houses, especially for weddings, with twigs and cotton-wrapped sticks and with pigments from turmeric, indigo, soot, flowers and clay. Its most striking habit is to leave no space empty: every figure is outlined and then filled with its own pattern of lines, dots, scales or waves. The program does this by colour. It reduces the picture to eight pigments and gives most of them a fill pattern.

The picture is blurred and snapped to the eight pigments (madder red, turmeric, leaf green, indigo, lamp black, paper, saffron and earth), cleaned with a majority filter and outlined in black wherever two colours meet. Inside each region a pattern is added, chosen by the pigment: a diamond lattice on red, dots on yellow, waves on green, fish-scale arcs on blue, dots in paper white on black, concentric rings on saffron and stripes in paper white on earth. The pattern repeats every q = 1.6 × size px, and its coordinates wobble with a sine wave so that the lines look drawn by hand. A border of triangles in four colours is set round the painting between rules of black.

equations.note: The lattice of diagonal lines in red regions. Lines of width 0.14 q in each of two directions, so about 1 − 0.86² ≈ 26% of the region is covered.
The dot pattern: a dot in every square. Its covering fraction φ is about 9%.
Concentric rings in saffron regions: five rings per unit of radius, each about a third of the ring spacing.
The fill line is blended with strength 0.9 κ, where κ is the pattern strength slider (0 to 1), so light lines are drawn on the dark pigments and dark lines on the others.

presets.text: Strong patterns make every colour its own texture.
Few colours and thick outlines read like a folk painting.
A wide border frames the picture like a wall painting.
